correctness.rationale: Reconstructed local vertex-star incidence proof for exactly eleven unit squares of the regular hyperbolic {4,5} tessellation: each interior vertex has five incident tiles, adjacent vertex stars intersect in two, opposite square corners in one. Every four distinct interior vertices require at least 12 tiles: for induced adjacency e<=2 the six-pair intersection sum is <=8; e=3 (path or 3-star) it remains <=8; e=4 forces a genuine square-face and its union has 13 tiles. Three centers with union <=11 must form a two-edge path; its endpoint neighbor-pairs occupy exactly two dihedral orbits in the five-cycle link. Both star-unions have exactly 11 tiles, are connected disk-like and have h=3. The published no-hole extremality theorem and edge/Euler relation e1=2n+2-2h give min e1=24-2(3)=18 and exactly two isometry types. This is a combinatorial edge perimeter, not hyperbolic length.
residual_risks: The proof relies on published no-hole minimality; did not independently rederive that general theorem.
The local face geometry and no-nonfacial-four-cycle condition are needed in this exact regular tiling; not generalized to other tilings.

value.rationale: The precise number of isometry classes of minimizers is an explicitly motivated exact invariant beyond the widely known isoperimetric minimum. This small natural count reveals the two local incidence configurations and supplies a rigorous benchmark for the open-ended study of extremal {p,q}-animal enumerations; it does not allege a full census.
residual_risks: Scope is a single small tile count; value is a localized sharp equality-class classification, not a broad tiling theorem.

limitations: Exactly 11 connected interior tiles in regular {4,5}; only combinatorial boundary-edge perimeter and full tessellation isometries.
